title: Cost law for the derandomized BLR program
statement: Let $n,r\ge0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $s:\{0,1\}^r\to\mathbb F_2^n$ be a seed map, and fix an input $b\in\{0,1\}^n$. Running the program that first draws a uniform seed, then tests the BLR relation using three queries to $f$ and charges $2n+1$ local work steps has the following joint law of output and cost: the seed is uniform on $\{0,1\}^r$, the output is the BLR decision on the corresponding binary inputs, and the cost is always $(0,3,r+(2n+1)+3)$, recording respectively random examples, queries, and work.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube
$s$ maps $r$ Boolean seed bits to the binary cube of dimension $n$
the input is a vector of $n$ Boolean bits
